sec: Sepsis treatment ladder & the SAFE trial note · p801

items.q: Match the treatment steps for sepsis-associated AKI — 1) First line  2) Second line  3) Third line  4) Fourth line … A) Cortisol  B) Vasopressor  C) Crystalloid  D) Dobutamine
items.exp: Treatment ladder for sepsis-AKI: crystalloid (1st line) → vasopressor (2nd line) with norepinephrine > dopamine → dobutamine → cortisol. (Book p801)

items.q: The first-line treatment for sepsis-associated AKI is:
opts: Crystalloid
Norepinephrine
Dobutamine
Cortisol
items.exp: Treatment: crystalloid (1st line) → vasopressor (2nd line) → dobutamine → cortisol. (Book p801)

items.q: A patient with septic shock remains hypotensive after adequate crystalloid. According to the ladder, the next agent is:
opts: Norepinephrine, which is preferred over dopamine
Dobutamine, which is preferred over norepinephrine
Cortisol as the second-line agent
Diuretics to improve urine output
items.exp: Second line: vasopressor — norepinephrine > dopamine; then dobutamine; then cortisol. (Book p801)

items.q: In sepsis-associated AKI, dopamine is preferred over norepinephrine as the vasopressor.
opts: False — the ladder states norepinephrine > dopamine
True — dopamine is preferred for its renal dose effect
True, but only with concomitant dobutamine
False — vasopressors are not used in sepsis at all
items.exp: The treatment ladder reads: vasopressor (2nd line) — norepinephrine > dopamine. (Book p801)

items.q: The trial quoted to establish the efficacy of crystalloids and colloids in sepsis is:
opts: SAFE trial — Saline versus Albumin Fluid Evaluation
SAFE trial — Sepsis and Antibiotics For Everyone
SOAP trial — Saline Or Albumin Protocol
ARISE trial — Albumin Resuscitation In Severe Endotoxaemia
items.exp: Note: efficacy of crystalloids & colloids established by the SAFE trial — Saline versus Albumin Fluid Evaluation. (Book p801)

items.q: Diuretics are not used in the prevention or treatment of AKI.
opts: True
False — diuretics are first line in AKI
False — diuretics are used only in prevention
True, but only in pre-renal AKI
items.exp: Note: diuretics are not used in the prevention or treatment of AKI — they do not improve renal recovery. (Book p801)

items.q: A resident suggests furosemide to 'convert oliguric AKI to non-oliguric AKI and improve outcome'. The correct response based on the note is:
opts: Diuretics are not used in prevention or treatment of AKI
Diuretics are the first-line treatment in AKI
Diuretics improve renal recovery if given early
Diuretics are indicated in all oliguric patients
items.exp: Note: diuretics not used in prevention or treatment of AKI. (Book p801)

items.q: The ultrasound figure labelled IVC on this page is used to assess:
opts: Volume status by measuring the IVC diameter — normal 2–2.5 cm
Renal size to exclude chronic kidney disease
Presence of renal calculi
Bladder residual volume
items.exp: The IVC ultrasound is shown to assess volume status; the normal IVC diameter is 2–2.5 cm and it determines the amount of fluid required. (Book p801)

items.q: In the passive leg raising figure, fluid is transferred from the legs and abdominal compartments. The stated purpose is:
opts: A test for fluid responsiveness (obsolete), with the VE 30 mL/kg challenge shown on the graph
A manoeuvre to increase renal perfusion permanently
A test for intra-abdominal hypertension
A test of cardiac ischaemia
items.exp: The PLR figure shows transfer of blood from the legs and abdominal compartments, labelled as a test for fluid responsiveness, with the 30 mL/kg VE (volume expansion) graph before and after. (Book p801)

items.q: All but one of the following appear in the sepsis-AKI treatment ladder. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Furosemide infusion
Crystalloid first line
Norepinephrine preferred over dopamine
Dobutamine
items.exp: The ladder is crystalloid → vasopressor (norepinephrine > dopamine) → dobutamine → cortisol; diuretics are explicitly not used in prevention or treatment of AKI. (Book p801)
